chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad, from Abdul Kareem, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

The waiting period of the woman who does not menstruate and the woman suffering from irregular bleeding from which she is not pure, is three months; and the waiting period of the woman who menstruates and her menstruation is regular, is three Quroo (pure periods), and Al-Quroo is the coagulation of the blood between the two menstruations.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman with irregular menstruation according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the foundational juristic distinction between 'Quroo’' (the interval of purity between two menstruations) and 'Taharah' (complete purity) to determine the Iddah for irregular menstruants. It clarifies that women with stable cycles observe three Quroo’, while those with irregular or absent menstruation observe three months, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise temporal markers in family law. This ruling is critical for determining the validity of remarriage and paternity lines in cases of menstrual uncertainty.
